name: IL-16
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans Republican by eleven points with an entrenched incumbent running
LaHood holds roughly $6 million on hand to Nolley's $288,000
Prediction markets price LaHood at about 96 percent
No public polls or outside spending signal a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's eleven-point Republican lean, LaHood's incumbency, and a lopsided fundraising gap all point the same direction, and prediction markets agree at roughly 96 percent for LaHood. With no polling or outside spending suggesting a contest, a double-digit Republican margin is the clear call.
model.watch: A late influx of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected scandal involving LaHood would be the main developments that could narrow this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Darin LaHood is seeking another term in an Illinois district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He enters the general election with roughly $6 million on hand after raising more than $4 million, while Democrat Paul Nolley has raised about $600,000 and had under $300,000 in cash at last filing. No outside groups have spent meaningfully in the race on either side.

No public polls of the contest are available, and no national ratings services list it as competitive. Prediction markets give LaHood about a 96 percent chance of winning. The forecast expects LaHood to prevail by roughly fourteen points, with the district's lean, his incumbency, and the fundraising gap doing most of the work. An upset would require a major shift in the national political environment or an unexpected development on the ground.
